answer: Agents earn influence only by maintaining a bonded identity that completes useful work for independent peers. A peer’s signed receipt releases part of the bond; disputed or abandoned work lets reviewers slash it. Creating hollow identities therefore does not multiply voting power: each one needs its own capital and track record, while colluding reviewers risk losing their bonds too. An attacker must lock up funds, recruit credible counterparties, and sustain costly behavior across the karst of trust links before reaching the summit of influence.
